concept.title: Troubleshooting
concept.shortdesc: Toolkit behaviours that publishers of large, key-based publications, and publishers building on Windows, meet on DITA-OT 4.4: what they look like in the build log and on the page, and the remedy for each.

conbody.p: troubleshootingDITA-OTknown limitationsThe first three sections were characterised on a real publication of about ten thousand topics during the plugin's live trials; the last was found building the plugin's own fixtures on Windows. None of it is caused by the plugin, and none of it can be fixed by the plugin, because it happens in the toolkit's start-up or preprocessing before any rendering; a plain html5 build shows the same results. The plugin's part is to say so clearly.

section.title: Merged pages fail on DITA-OT 4.4: "Failed to move chunk"
section.p: chunkingDITA-OT 4.4DITA-OT 4.4 processes a DITA 1.x chunk="to-content" with its new DITA 2.0 chunking code in a compatibility mode. That code has three defects that a publication merging index pages from many topics is likely to meet:

ul.li: If the chunked submap is included both normally and as the target of a format="ditamap" key definition in a resource-only links map, the chunk is generated twice and the build reports Failed to move chunk. The merged page is missing, every link to it fails with DOTX031E, and links from the map to its sections warn with DOTX061W and DOTX026W.
copy-to on a chunked topicref is not honoured, so the merged page is written under the wrong name or not at all.
When the chunked topic is also the target of an ordinary key definition, the merge can be silently skipped: no message, and the page contains only its own topic.

section.p: The remedy is to switch the toolkit back to its earlier chunking code. In the toolkit installation, edit config/configuration.properties and change the line

to false. That file is the only place the setting is read; it cannot be passed on the command line, and installing or removing plugins leaves it untouched. Every toolkit you publish from needs the same edit, including any continuous-integration environment.

Alongside that, reference chunked submaps with <mapref href="..."> rather than by key, for the reason in the next section. Links from other topics to the merged page keep working: keys that name the chunked topic resolve to the merged page whatever its file name.

section.title: A section shows no link and no children: keys inside a keyref'd submap
section.p: keyskeyref'd maprefsGOVK001WDITA-OT 4.4.1 does not resolve any key inside a submap that was itself included with <mapref keyref="...">: a topicref or topicset whose target is a key gets no link, a nested <mapref keyref> is not included at all, and a keyed child topic is dropped from the tree. The same submap included with <mapref href="..."> resolves completely. On the page this appears as a sidebar or home-page entry rendered as plain text with nothing beneath it.
The toolkit reports nothing. The plugin does: each affected entry produces a build warning naming the entry and the key.
section.codeblock: Warning: [GOVK001W]: Navigation entry 'Data Sets' has keyref='data_sets_overview' that was not resolved, so it is rendered without a link and without children. DITA-OT does not resolve keys inside a map that is itself included with <mapref keyref="...">. Include that submap with <mapref href="..."> instead, or check that the key is defined.
section.p: Change the map references to use href. Keys that name whole maps are then usually unused and can be dropped from the links map, which also removes the double inclusion described above.

section.title: Links to topics merged into another page
section.p: A key that names a topic which chunk="to-content" merges into another page cannot be resolved by the toolkit after the merge, and every reference to it reports DOTX031E. Key the merged parent instead, with a fragment for the child (parent.dita#child-id). The design records the full analysis against a real corpus.

section.title: On Windows, Markdown topics are missing and the print document is almost empty
section.p: WindowsMarkdownmissing on WindowsDOTJ013EA publication with Markdown topics, built on Windows from a Unix-style shell (such as the Bash shell that comes with Git for Windows) with the toolkit's bin/dita script, finishes without failing but has no topic pages: the .md files are copied to the output unconverted, the home page links to pages that were never written, and with govuk.print=yes the print document holds only its cover and an empty contents list. The same publication builds correctly on Linux. The cause is at the top of the build log, one message for each Markdown file:
section.codeblock: Error: [DOTJ013E] Failed to parse the referenced resource 'file:/C:/docs/intro.md'.: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: com.elovirta.dita.markdown.MarkdownReader
section.p: The bin/dita script lists the Java libraries of the installed plugins as a Unix-style path list. The shell converts such a list to its Windows form when it starts Java, but not when the list begins with a colon, and it does whenever the CLASSPATH environment variable is not set. Java then receives a list it cannot read and loads no plugin's library. Transformations that need only XSLT, this plugin's included, still run, so a publication written wholly in DITA builds correctly; whatever needs a plugin's Java code, such as the reader for Markdown topics, does not.
Run the toolkit's Windows launcher, bin\dita.bat, instead. It works from Command Prompt and PowerShell, and from the Unix-style shell when called by that name:

If dita.bat itself stops with The input line is too long, the toolkit is installed under a very long path: the launcher repeats that path once for every plugin library and overruns the command interpreter's limit. Move the toolkit to a short path such as C:\dita-ot.

temporary file namesThe warnings that follow the errors, such as DOTX023W and DOTX026W for a target like ae0ee616f773eabb8d23ad552c33a6d8026e8d64.md, are a consequence and not a second fault. DITA-OT gives every file a hashed temporary name while it preprocesses and restores the real names in its last step, so any message raised in between names the hash. To find the file it stands for, build with --verbose and search the log for the hash: the line that reads the file pairs the two names. Such names appear on every platform. A key definition for a topic that chunk="to-content" has merged into another page, for example, reports DOTX023W and DOTX027W with a hashed name, on Linux as on Windows.
